collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult and a builder or another adult; in the story (name1) uses a wheelchair)

collection.description: A villager whose wheelchair sinks in the sand has drawn wider wheels: build it their way, or try the builder's idea first.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject)'s wheelchair is a good one: a sturdy wooden seat, two big wheels on a proper axle, two little ones in front. It's perfect on the packed paths of the village. On the beach it's hopeless. The thin wheels dig into the sand and stop dead. (subject) wants to go fishing from the beach like everyone else, and has drawn a design in the sand for wider wheels. (friend) is looking at the drawing doubtfully.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (friend) suggests a few changes. (subject) explains, patiently and then less patiently, why each of them won't work. In the end they build it (subject)'s way: wide rims of bent wood wrapped in woven palm. The first try on the sand, the chair rolls straight down to the water's edge. (subject) whoops so loudly the fishers turn around. (friend) admits (friend.he/she) should probably have listened sooner.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: They try (friend)'s idea: planks laid across the sand like a path. It works, sort of. It takes ages to lay the planks and the tide keeps moving them. By the third day (friend) gives up and helps build (subject)'s wide wheels after all. They work beautifully. "You could have just said," says (friend). "I did," says (subject). "Several times."
